summary.headline: Harshdeep Hortico H2 FY26 revenue rose to INR 36.1 crore-range with EBITDA of INR 11.3 crore, but FY26 revenue of INR 69 crore missed the INR 85 crore internal expectation.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 H1 revenue of about INR 32.64 crore and H2 of about INR 36.1 crore, versus INR 24.9 crore and INR 31.51 crore in FY25. EBITDA rose to INR 8.4 crore in H1 and INR 11.3 crore in H2 (from INR 5.95 crore and INR 9.0 crore), and PAT to INR 5.7 crore and INR 6.82 crore. The CFO said full-year revenue of INR 69 crore fell short of the INR 85 crore expectation because of LPG gas cuts of about two months, raw material (PP) prices up 20-25% or more, and deferred luxury orders. Management said demand is holding flat year-on-year but not growing, and that margins are being defended by passing on only part of the cost increase.

segments.name: Roto moulded series
segments.commentary: About 30.66% of FY26 revenue per management; described as the highest-quality, high-volume, high-margin category with about 10-year warranty. Management said this segment was hit hardest by the price-driven slowdown.

segments.name: Grower series (injection moulded nursery pots)
segments.commentary: Described as about 30-40% of revenue and 42-43% of margins; high volume, low margin, about 1 lakh pots per day. Management said demand is not materially affected, with about 10-15% growth in the segment.

segments.name: Decorative series
segments.commentary: About 14% of revenue; affected by deferred purchases alongside roto moulded products.

segments.name: AgriShield shade nets
segments.commentary: Introduced in FY26; about 3% of revenue. Management guided to roughly 10-20% growth and said capacity at 100% efficiency, with the Pune line fully booked.

segments.name: Fiberglass, EcoSeries, garden furniture and fountains
segments.commentary: Fiberglass about 3.78%, EcoSeries about 1-2%, garden furniture about 1%. Roto moulded fountains launched in March 2026 with a 10-year warranty, and management reported 15-20 days of order backlog.

segments.name: Channel mix
segments.commentary: B2B about 75% and B2C about 25% per one answer; later a B2C ballpark of 15-18% of current revenue excluding wholesaler sales. Management said 13 major distributors and seven showrooms, mainly for wholesalers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance of INR 115 crore was referenced by an analyst; management did not confirm a firm number and avoided giving one.
Management said 25-30% annual growth is achievable if geopolitical conditions normalise.
Management said the current infrastructure can support revenue above INR 100 crore, and claimed comfort with 35-40% growth from existing capacity.
Management said it will hold margins as far as possible and expects to pass on only part of the cost increase.
Next detailed commentary expected after H1 FY27 results; no formal con-call scheduled before then.
capex_capacity: Three factories: Bhiwandi (about 1 lakh sq ft, largest), Pune (about 40,000 sq ft) and Delhi (about 20,000-25,000 sq ft, newly added this year).
Two warehouses (Bhiwandi and Bangalore), with an added Pune warehouse and a Kolkata warehouse serving the Northeast.
About 10% of facility capacity affected by raw material and LPG shortages, per management.
Solar panels installed on the Pune factory; management expects savings of about INR 10-15 lakh per month, MW capacity not disclosed.
No FY27 capex plans announced; management said it is comfortable and would discuss any future capex.
demand_pricing: Raw material (PP) prices up about 60% per management, from INR 100-120/kg to INR 160-170 (some grades INR 220); company passed on about 20-25% in wholesale prices, with competitors at 25-30%.
Customers are holding back orders; management said April-May sales are flat year-on-year with no decline and no exponential growth.
Current order book: three airport orders (Lucknow, Mumbai, Visakhapatnam) worth about INR 1.5 crore, plus ongoing showroom orders.
Ugaoo is the largest customer, at about 10% of business, up from about INR 1 crore to about INR 10 crore this year.
Export share about 2% of revenue; new export markets in Canada, USA and the Netherlands this year.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue mix between B2B and B2C, and whether B2B is order-book driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B is about 75% and B2C about 25%, with pots purely B2B and garden furniture and fountains sold B2C. Current order book was about INR 1.5 crore of airport orders.

qa_highlights.question: Realistic FY27 revenue and three-year growth aspiration after the FY26 shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a firm number, citing LPG cuts, labour shortage, raw material spikes and deferred projects. It said 25-30% annual growth is realistic if conditions normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold around 30% after raw material inflation, and has price been raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices were raised about 20-25% on wholesale rates (not MRP), with the company holding back on full pass-through to avoid losing customers. Management said it will keep margins as high as possible.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rising YoY, and what is the sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to inventory build for capacity growth and sudden orders (e.g., about INR 1 crore in two weeks for an event), plus credit to large customers and new stores. It gave no target number.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory (up 62%) and receivables (up 51%) growth due to pre-stocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no pre-stocking; it held stock for only 15-20 working days during raw material shortages and expects the condition to be temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H2 EBITDA margin about 31% vs about 28% last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality, with H2 driven by festivals and landscaping projects and higher-margin roto moulded and decorative products, plus the new fountain launch.

qa_highlights.question: How are large B2B and infra orders won, and what is the margin differential versus distributors?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders come through landscapers and subcontractors who tender on the company's behalf, as payment security is needed. Management said distributor and project margins are the same, with discounts of 45-50% based on order value, and the project margin is about 17%.

risks_watch: Raw material (PP) and LPG availability: about two months of LPG disruption and about 10% of capacity affected per management.
Working capital stress: inventory up 62% and receivables up 51% YoY, with credit extended to large customers.
Demand softness in roto moulded and decorative series as customers defer discretionary spend; FY27 growth targets unconfirmed.
Fuel and transport cost increases (about 10-15% extra per management) could further squeeze margins or demand.
Customer concentration: Ugaoo at about 10% of revenue, and reliance on a few large infra projects that management said have been deferred.
Disclosure gaps: solar capacity (MW), B2C split including wholesalers, and export data were not provided; the company said it would revert by email.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the H2 earnings and long-term growth, but noticeably cautious and evasive on FY27 numbers, raw material pass-through, and the B2C split. Management repeatedly said it cannot quantify near-term growth until H1 FY27 results.
key_quotes: We are comfortable to do at least 35-40% growth from the current infrastructure.
So, there is no dip in the business as of now because of all these conditions, but we are not seeing any exponential growth as well.
Distributor margins and the big project margins are the same. We don't differentiate in any much way.
